findings.evidence: replacing the current fine notices with automatic email reminders sent three, seven, and fourteen days after the due date
findings.fix: State explicitly whether the piloted branches used this same reminder cadence, and if they did not, either cite separate evidence for this specific schedule's effectiveness or present the cadence as an untested implementation detail rather than as part of the evidenced recommendation.
findings.violation: TOULMIN-GROUNDS requires each claim the argument advances to be attached to checkable evidence rather than asserted outright. The specific three/seven/fourteen-day email reminder cadence is presented as part of the recommended change, but nothing in the pilot description (What the Pilot Showed) states that this reminder schedule, or any reminder schedule, was part of what was piloted, so there is no evidence tying the measured 94-percent return rate to this particular notification design.

findings.evidence: This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date; items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established.
findings.fix: Either cite the specific pilot statistic that shows returns clustering within 60 days (for example, the share of eventual returns completed by day 60), or drop the claim that the cutoff matches an established pattern and instead state the 60-day window as a policy choice made independently of the pilot data.
findings.violation: TOULMIN-GROUNDS requires a claim to be attached to evidence a reader could check. This sentence asserts the 60-day cutoff matches a pattern the pilot data established, but the pilot section (What the Pilot Showed) reports only an aggregate 16-month on-time-or-eventual return rate and never breaks that figure down by any time window, so there is no pilot figure a reader can check this specific 60-day boundary against.

findings.evidence: Consortium finance records show fine revenue covered under 2 percent of the annual materials budget over the last three fiscal years, and the four pilot branches absorbed the loss without a measurable change to their replacement-copy spending, so the shortfall the objection anticipates has not materialized where the policy has already been tried.
findings.fix: Add a sentence addressing why a partial or reduced-fine policy was not recommended instead of full elimination, for example by noting whether the pilot or the cited research brief distinguishes partial fee reduction from full elimination, or by stating why full elimination was judged necessary rather than sufficient.
findings.violation: TOULMIN-REBUTTAL requires the argument to name and address the conditions its own grounds leave open. The pilot design described in What the Pilot Showed is binary (fines eliminated versus fines kept), which leaves open whether a reduced-fine policy, rather than full elimination, could have captured a similar share of the return-rate and avoidance-survey gains at less revenue cost. The artifact answers the full-elimination-versus-status-quo revenue objection but never raises or answers this reduced-fee alternative, which its own pilot design directly leaves open.
